# 30 — `maps/empty16x.i3d` (scene graph)

The i3d is the scene: the terrain plus the camera/light/spawn nodes. GIANTS i3d is XML (schema
`http://i3d.giants.ch/schema/i3d-1.6.xsd`). Generated by `tools/gen_i3d.py`. The terrain node itself is big
enough to have its own doc — see **31_terrain_node.md**.

## Top-level structure

```xml
<i3D name="empty16x.i3d" version="1.6" xmlns:xsi="..." xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="...i3d-1.6.xsd">
  <Asset><Export program="fs25-empty-map/gen_i3d.py" version="1.0" /></Asset>
  <Files>      <File fileId="N" filename="..." /> ...   </Files>
  <Materials>  <Material .../> ...                       </Materials>
  <Scene>      camera, sun, terrain, spawn, ...          </Scene>
</i3D>
```

## Sections

- **`<Files>`** — the fileId→filename table every node references by id. Two kinds:
  - `$data/...` / `$dataS/...` = base-game engine assets (shaders, ground textures, `groundHeightNoise`,
    `infoLayer_environment`). Referenceable; carry no map data.
  - `data/...` = **map-local files our generators produce** (DEM, weights, densities, infolayers).
  We assign our own fileIds sequentially and de-duplicate (many DistanceTextures point at one texture).

- **`<Materials>`** — 2 materials:
  - `terrainMaterial_mat` (materialId 1) → `$data/shaders/terrainShader.xml`.
  - `groundDetailHeight_mat` (materialId 2) → `$data/shaders/groundHeightShader.xml` + dummy fill textures +
    `heightNoiseMap` custom map. Used by the `terrainDetailHeight` layer.

- **`<Scene>`** — node order we emit:
  1. `Camera name="persp"` — default perspective camera.
  2. `Light name="sun"` — directional sun (shadow-map params). Required for lighting.
  3. `TerrainTransformGroup name="terrain"` — the map (see 31).
  4. `Camera name="cameraOverView"` — top-down overview camera.
  5. `TransformGroup name="careerStartPoint"` — the new-game spawn point (`translation` above the surface;
     flat terrain ~39 m so we spawn at y=42).
  6. `TransformGroup name="gameplay"` — empty container (base maps hang selling/animal triggers here).

## Key fact: NO Shapes, NO `.i3d.shapes`
An empty flat map has **no meshes** — the terrain is heightmap-driven, and we omit all gameplay trigger/marker
`<Shape>`s. So there is no `externalShapesFile`, no `.i3d.shapes` sidecar. (Shapes are geometry stored in the
binary `.i3d.shapes`; needing one would pull in that whole format.)

## Encoding
Written `iso-8859-1` with XML declaration (matches GIANTS tooling). `ET.indent` for readability.
